Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m using the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill because this change depends on inspecting the current multi-wake rollout evidence before touching the target policy. I’ll first read the workspace contract and the skill instructions, then trace the assigned parent, sampled results, and inherited logs before producing the single candidate and both required documentation updates.

The workspace contract confirms that the candidate must stay materializable throughout, and that the visual diagnosis must be written before any policy edit. I’m now inventorying the complete parent/sample evidence and will compare the best finite sample against the most informative failure, including both keyframe sheets and their metric traces.

The visual comparison shows a common failure topology: every sampled controller generates a real upstream leg, then curves upward and exits while still roughly 6.6–6.7 L from the target, never reaching the developed wake corridor. The `-0.25` rearward-bearing reversal is the strongest finite sample and avoids exact anterior speed-cap contact, while disabling rearward bearing and adding damping repeats the same turn sooner; I’m checking the inherited ablation notes now to isolate a single next mechanism rather than bundling unrelated retuning.

The inherited notes and current rollout close the obvious nearby alternatives: corrections active from release, damping interpolation, steering-ceiling changes, and zero rearward bearing all preserve the failure or damage the useful leg. I’ve recorded the pre-edit diagnosis; the candidate will now preserve the entire best target-ahead controller and make one isolated change—rearward bearing authority from `-0.25` to `-0.50`—with explicit load and trajectory falsification limits.

The material-guidance check passes: the notes exist and the experience bank differs semantically from the assigned parent. I’m running the remaining non-CFD contract and editable-boundary checks now, including the deterministic parameter-schema guard.

Produced exactly one complete multi-wake candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:11) preserves the best sampled target-ahead controller and changes only rearward bearing authority from `-0.25` to `-0.50`.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) records the keyframe/metrics diagnosis and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:96) adds the evidence-backed rearward-countersteer lesson and prunes stale next-test advice.

Checks: guidance PASS, editable boundary PASS, parameter schema PASS (`17/17`). Julia smoke was unavailable because Julia is not installed. CFD was intentionally not run.
